elements.scope_reason: Red-box header: urgent attention for the health worker with occupational stress and any of the four items. The house standard encodes this as an Urgent priority evaluation of the form (and <presenting complaint> (or ...)).
elements.problem: Trigger 'occupational stress' is encoded as (snomed_concept "Stress at work" "finding") (SNOMED 276074009, child of Stress and Problems at work), which matches the page's meaning. Note 'Stress at work' is not a recorded common symptom or warning sign, so the rule depends on that finding being recorded first (see rule-level problems).

elements.scope_reason: Red-box criterion with two parts: alcohol intoxication; drug intoxication; plus the context 'at work'.
elements.problem: Both parts are covered by the single concept 'Intoxication caused by psychoactive substance' (disorder): 'Alcohol intoxication' is a direct child (is_a confirmed) and the drug intoxications (cocaine, cannabis, hallucinogen, stimulant, hypnotic, anxiolytic, opioid poisonings) are its other children, and descendants match automatically in due_to. The context 'at work' has no representation in the language; this is a limitation, not a builder error, and the 'Stress at work' trigger carries the occupational context. The item appears in both the check_for and the priority rule.

elements.scope_reason: Screening column 'Possible alcohol or drug problem' with its criteria: a conclusion ('possible X') plus discriminating findings the house standard puts in check_for and a possible diagnosis rule. Parts: (a) >= 4 drinks/session in the past year, (b) illegal drug use in the past year, (c) misused prescription or OTC medication in the past year, (d) smells of alcohol, (e) conclusion 'possible alcohol or drug problem'.
parts_missing: Time window 'in the past year' for (a)-(c): not encoded (an onset comparison such as (< (onset ...) (time_ago 1 year)) is available in due_to but was not used; arguably not_representable in check_for)

The threshold '>= 4 drinks per session' is approximated by the concept 'Heavy drinking session' with no number; the language has no drink-count unit, so this is the best available approximation and is acceptable

The column's specific mapping (alcohol/drug findings -> possible alcohol or drug problem) is not preserved: the substance-misuse rule fires on any item from any of the five columns (e.g. Fatigue alone), see rule-level problems

The conclusion is encoded as possible 'Substance misuse behavior' (finding, 415658005), a reasonable match for 'alcohol or drug problem' / 'substance misuse'. What is lost is the column structure: the rule's evidence is the full list of all 19 screening findings rather than this column's four.

rule_level_problems.rule: Diagnose possible substance misuse / depression / anxiety / burnout in health worker with occupational stress
rule_level_problems.problem: The four possible-diagnosis rules are byte-identical in their evidence: (and Stress-at-work (or <all 19 screening findings>)). The page's column structure is flattened away, so 'Fatigue' alone yields possible substance misuse, depression, anxiety and burnout at once, and the column heading 'Possible alcohol or drug problem' (which is itself a 'possible X' conclusion attached to only its own four findings) is not preserved. The footer's 'any of the above may have ...' justifies a broad reading, but a closer encoding would evidence substance misuse from the alcohol/drug column (with the others as broad fallbacks) so the specific conclusion the page draws is kept.

rule_level_problems.rule: Check for urgent features and signs of occupational stress in the health worker (check_for)
rule_level_problems.problem: Two screening items are absent from the check_for and therefore from every rule: 'Diagnosis of long-term condition' (representable, e.g. Chronic disease + New qualifier) and 'Frequent lateness' (no SNOMED concept found; a not_representable note is the appropriate handling).
The footer names five conclusions (substance misuse, stress, depression, anxiety, burnout); 'stress' has no possible-diagnosis rule. Low because the trigger is already 'Stress at work'.

Every rule is anchored on (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Stress at work" "finding")), which is not a recorded common symptom or warning sign, and nothing else on the page records it. The page is also about the health worker, not the patient, so whether these rules can ever fire in a patient encounter is a question for the clinician/remaining-questions file. Not a wrong encoding, but the house standard asks for this to be flagged.

rule_level_problems.rule: Urgent: health worker with occupational stress ... (red box)
rule_level_problems.problem: All four red-box criteria are qualified 'at work' on the page; no item carries that context. The language has no clean way to express it (an 'Occupational' qualifier value exists but is not an established pattern), so this is a limitation to record rather than an error.
An 'event'-category concept inside clinical_finding. The grammar's category validator accepts it, but no gold-standard rule does this; confirm the runtime records and matches it.

summary: The red box is encoded correctly and completely: Urgent priority, trigger 'Stress at work', and all four criteria (both halves of each compound item) with well-chosen concepts that exist and cover alcohol and drug intoxication through SNOMED descendants. The main weakness is in the screening section: two items are missing from the check_for ('Diagnosis of long-term condition', which is representable, and 'Frequent lateness', which has no SNOMED concept), and the four possible-diagnosis rules share one flattened evidence list so the page's column-specific conclusion 'Possible alcohol or drug problem' is lost and any single item fires all four diagnoses. A 'stress' conclusion from the footer is not encoded, and the 'at work' and 'past year/month' qualifiers are unrepresented limitations rather than errors.
